summary: Implemented the FAWE-side PolymerEditBridge against Polymer's now-accepted public bulk-edit API, added an explicit direct-section route discriminator, and made prepare refusals surface as explicit REFUSED results that name the chunk/position and reason. The Fabric module compiles and packages, the bridge compiles against the exact polymer-common jar nested in the accepted bundle, and test/candidate-manifest.json pins a polymer profile with the accepted bundle. The combined run against f20e43c1 passed the direct-section success phases (sections=3, fallbackWrites=0, sent=3, relit=3); the manual-attachment and quarantined-chunk refusal records remain pending. Full S7 remains unaccepted.

discoveryTopology.reason: isModLoaded("polymer-core") is true; common is on core's runtime classpath; core and VE participants are present.

The bundle is the only supported install for this stage. A common-only deployment contains no PolymerBlock mappings (core) and no BlockWithElementHolder API (VE), so no Polymer state or holders can exist and a token would have nothing to reconcile. The bridge's absence is therefore safe, not a reconciliation gap.

VE depends only on common, so core-free VE deployments are valid and holders can exist. EditIntegrations.directSectionRouteSupported() returns false in this topology, so FabricCommitCoordinator disables whole-section publication and every cell goes through the ordinary lifecycle path (vanilla setBlockState hooks run). The bridge stays fail-closed, but holders cannot silently go stale. Any-of discovery (polymer-core OR polymer-virtual-entity) remains future work; the current Map<mod, impl> shape would double-register the same provider id and trip validate().

sourceChanges.summary: Owner-thread Polymer reservation: detached construction, prepare only for the direct-section route, reconcile actual committed changes against the FAWE receipt, publish after lighting and recipient sends, close exactly once on the owner thread, and refuse off-thread discard of a live token. Prepare refusals fail before any write with explicit no-writes/reload guidance, naming the chunk, the first proposed position and the concrete reason (unsupported attachment, Immersive Portals, section limit or unloaded chunk). Non-block payloads never acquire a token.

Added a provider veto, allowsDirectSections(level, authorized), and a route-aware beforePublication(level, authorized, directSections). The legacy two-argument hook remains source-compatible, is now default-empty, and is delegated to by the three-argument default.

Added owner-thread directSectionEligible (BLOCK only, no block entity on either side, one loaded chunk, minecraft-namespace-only sections) and made writeUnit take an explicit route. The strict route rechecks lifecycle cells, refuses lost eligibility, and never silently falls back while a provider holds section-scoped state; the ordinary route writes every cell through the existing lifecycle path. The lifecycle allowlist now includes the S7 fixture's birch_log, stripped_oak_log, acacia_log, jungle_log and redstone_lamp states; the combined run found the original allowlist refused them before write.

Computes the direct-section route after authorization, requires EditIntegrations.directSectionRouteSupported() (VE-without-core guard), requires every reservation to allow it, passes the route to beforePublication, and passes it to writeUnit. Native/WNA mutations never enter the direct-section route or acquire a Polymer token. Preparation failures now preserve the integration refusal text in the terminal receipt, and the quarantined-chunk message names the chunk.

fawe-coordinated now reports a clean pre-write refusal as REFUSED with the failing chunk and the bridge's reason, instead of the generic failed-after-N wording. Only FAILED_BEFORE_WRITE with no recorded changes is labelled REFUSED; partial and post-write failures keep the failed-after-N wording so a user-level retry cannot silently duplicate earlier units.

Added directSectionRouteSupported(): whole-section publication is disabled when polymer-virtual-entity is installed without polymer-core, because holders can exist while the bridge is not discovered. The guard forces the ordinary per-cell lifecycle, which still runs vanilla setBlockState hooks.

Added `fawepublish stats`, returning FabricEdits.publicationStatistics() as JSON. The combined S7 probe uses it to prove the direct-section route ran (sections incremented, fallbackWrites unchanged) instead of inferring the route from world state.
Compile-time signature mirror of the accepted public API. The mirror is a separate source set, never packaged, and not on the runtime classpath; real classes come from polymer-common at runtime.
Wired the polymerApiStub source set into compileJava as compileOnly output and made compileJava depend on the stub classes.

routeSemantics: Preparation remains detached and performs no live chunk or Polymer API access.
The coordinator authorizes every delta, then checks the static route-support guard and computes directSectionEligible over the whole final authorized set.

The static guard disables the direct-section route when polymer-virtual-entity is installed without polymer-core, because holders can exist while the bridge is not discovered; ordinary per-cell writes still run the vanilla lifecycle hooks.
If eligible, every reservation is consulted through allowsDirectSections; any false veto forces the ordinary per-cell route for the entire proposal.
The direct route acquires the Polymer token in beforePublication, replaces whole sections without calling LevelChunk.setBlockState, and does not mix ordinary or native writes while the token is live.

A prepare refusal (unsupported attachment, Immersive Portals, reserved/quarantined chunk, or unloaded chunk) fails the unit before any write with an explicit no-writes message naming the chunk, the first proposed position and the reason. The operation is not retried and the coordinator never switches routes mid-publication; unload/reload is required when the chunk is quarantined or no longer the loaded instance.

fawe-coordinated reports a FAILED_BEFORE_WRITE result with zero recorded changes as REFUSED for chunk X,Z plus the integration reason. Partial or post-write failures keep the failed-after-N wording so a user-level retry cannot duplicate earlier units. This is a wording change only; refusal, retry and route-selection semantics are unchanged.
Non-block and lifecycle-heavy proposals do not acquire a Polymer token; they remain transparent to Polymer.
Polymer refuses more than sixteen sections; FAWE vetoes the direct route before prepare in that case.
contractAdherence: prepare(LevelChunk, Set<Integer>, Map<BlockPos, BlockState>) is called on the owner thread immediately before the non-yielding direct-section writes, using the exact loaded chunk, absolute section Y numbers, and immutable proposed native states.
No yield occurs between prepare, section installation, and token.reconcile; reconcile is invoked even for partial applied results.

token.reconcile() returns Polymer's independently observed actual changes; the bridge compares them with CommitReceipt.applied() by position, state id, and canonical NBT. Disagreement is a finalization failure and is never retried.
The bridge strips Polymer's keepPacked marker before comparing block-entity NBT so the comparison matches FAWE's full-metadata receipt payload.
Lighting is awaited through FabricWorldAccess.completePublication before token.publish(). token.publish() runs on the owner thread after that wait.
token.close() is called exactly once on the owner thread from the coordinator's finish path; successful publication is idempotent.
A live token cannot reach off-thread discard; discard refuses it. Shutdown before publication closes on the owner thread.
The bridge uses only the public API surface described by handoff/s7-polymer/api-contract.json; no Polymer private holder map or mixin state is reflected.

Combined success-path run is in flight in the Polymer session's test/bulk harness with white-list=false and -Dfawe.experimental.coordinated=true. Content is oak_log at 3200,80,3200, lit lamp at 3201,80,3200, and birch_log at 3202,80,3200. Phases: set stone, set oak_log (fresh holders), set stripped_oak_log (identity retention). `fawepublish stats` must show sections==3 and fallbackWrites==0, with sent>=3; relit is informational because cells without light sources may legitimately skip relighting. No ERROR or mixin failures are allowed.

The refusal and quarantined-chunk phases still need a clean record.

Native-driver command packets are parsed verbatim by ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.parseCommand in 26.3: vanilla literals are slash-less (`setblock`), WorldEdit/FAWE registers both `pos1` and `/pos1`, and `fawe-coordinated` is slash-less. Do not send `/setblock` or `/fawe-coordinated` through the native command action.

Fixture note: RedstoneLampBlock has no onPlace override; an unpowered lit lamp schedules its 4-tick extinguish only from neighborChanged, and tick then cycles LIT off. Place the lamp last (or power it) so later adjacent placements do not neighbor-update it. A 14 -> 0 drop between snapshots is vanilla block ticking, not FAWE or Polymer; direct section swaps bypass neighbor updates and do not re-trigger it. `forceLightUpdates` only drives Polymer's forced-light indexing, not the vanilla block tick.
The combined probe is not a full S7 acceptance run; it exercises the direct-section success path, holder lifecycle and identity retention with the installed accepted bundle.
